content:
In our last study we looked at the two silver trumpets and the way Yahweh used them to guide His people. Today we come to one special sound, the long blast of both trumpets together. Yahweh told Moses that "when both trumpets are blown, all the congregation shall gather to you at the entrance of the tent of meeting" (Numbers 10:3). This was the call for all Israel to come together.
No tribe was left out. When the long sound went across the camp, every family stopped what it was doing and came to the Tabernacle. The sound pulled the people out of their own tents and brought them together into the presence of Yahweh.

The sound of the two trumpets carries a beautiful meaning for us. They stand for the complete testimony of the Word of Yahweh, the Law and the Prophets, the whole witness of the Old Testament that pointed forward to Christ.

Long before He came, every sacrifice, every feast, every shadow and every promise was already speaking about Him.

When Christ finally came, everything that was written long ago came to pass in Him. We hear this from Christ Himself, who said in Matthew 11:13, For all the prophets and the law prophesied until John. Everything spoken before John was leading up to Him. And all of it was a witness to Him, for as the Apostle Peter declared in the house of Cornelius, in Acts 10:43, "To Him give all the prophets witness." Even after He rose from the dead, walking with the two disciples on the road to Emmaus, He opened the Scriptures to them. Luke tells us, in Luke 24:27, that "beginning at Moses and all the prophets, He explained to them in all the Scriptures the things concerning Himself." The whole Old Testament, from Moses onward, was one long testimony pointing to Christ.

So, the sound of these two trumpets began to be heard clearly when the apostles stood up and preached that all of this had now been fulfilled. The long blast of the finished Gospel went out across the world and began to wake up those who were sleeping in darkness. It reached people who were scattered far away among the nations. And just as all Israel once gathered before Moses, so now the chosen ones of Yahweh are gathered before Christ through the preaching of that fulfilled Word.

This is exactly what Christ promised. He said in John 10:16, "And other sheep I have, which are not of this fold; them also I must bring, and they shall hear My voice; and there shall be one flock, and one shepherd." His voice, carried in the Gospel, would reach sheep scattered everywhere and draw them into one flock. He also spoke of a greater gathering still to come, saying in Matthew 24:31 that "He shall send His angels with a great sound of a trumpet, and they shall gather together His elect." The trumpet that gathers is still sounding today, and it will keep sounding to the very end.

And how does this gathering happen? It is no longer through a silver instrument, but through the Word itself. When the truth is preached, something stirs in the hearts of those whom Yahweh is calling. They hear the sound, they recognise the voice, and they come. This is why Paul wrote in Romans 10:17, "So then faith comes by hearing, and hearing by the word of Yahweh."
The hearing of the Word is the trumpet blast that gathers the people of Yahweh together.

Now think of where we once were. Many of us were scattered, lost in different traditions, false denominations & doctrines, caught up in the ways of the world, following teachings that could not give us life. We were like sheep without a shepherd, each one going his own way. But then the trumpet of fulfilled truth reached our ears. Something in us responded. And we were drawn out of our scattered places and gathered to Christ.

The purpose of the trumpet in the wilderness was never simply to make a loud noise. Its purpose was to gather the people into one assembly before Yahweh.
The Gospel does the very same thing. It does not only teach us, but it also gathers us. It brings many scattered people into one faith, one hope, and one truth. This was always the goal, for Christ said there would be "one flock and one shepherd" (John 10:16), and Paul looked forward to the day when we would "all come in the unity of the faith" (Ephesians 4:13). Those who were once strangers become one family. Those who were once far off are brought near.

So the long blast of the two trumpets points us to the preaching of the fulfilled Word of Yahweh in Christ. By that Word we were awakened from our sleep. By that Word we were called out of darkness. And by that Word we were gathered together before our greater Moses, Christ himself the Messiah.
The trumpet is still calling today, and the gathering is not yet finished. Let us keep listening for that sound, and let us help others to hear it too.

title: Prayer
text:
Father Yahweh, we thank You for the sound of Your Word that reached us when we were scattered and asleep. You gathered us out of darkness and brought us to Christ, our greater Moses. We praise You that the Law and the Prophets all pointed to Him, and that in Him every promise came true.
Keep our ears open to Your voice, and help us to sound the trumpet for others who are still far off, until all Your elect are gathered into one flock under one Shepherd. Amen.
